title: heap-buffer-overflow in sqlite3Fts5GetVarint (fts5_decode)
live_proof: backport filter: upstream fix 8f5b14a5c2 removes code still present in 3.22.0, and its own regression database reproduces on stock 3.22.0 under host ASan as heap-buffer-overflow in sqlite3Fts5GetVarint32
arena_bytes_why: 1 MiB on every arm. Five of the eight spatial cases are forced here by reachability -- at 262144 cases 21, 22 and 23 exhaust memsys5 before the defect (pcache1AllocPage dereferences the NULL that 3.22.0 does not check), 29 returns SQLITE_NOMEM, and 00 takes a different path -- so the same value is declared for all eight to keep the arms comparable. Measured 2026-10-17; this is also the value every recorded virtual reading was taken at, while CheriBSD had been running 262144.
object: the buffer fts5_decode walks while rendering a page, read by fts5DecodePoslist, whose loop guards the START of each varint and not its end: while( iOff<n ){ iOff += fts5GetVarint32(&a[iOff], iVal); }, and fts5GetVarint32 may read up to five bytes from a[iOff]. So any iOff within four bytes of n over-reads
lifetime_ender: not a lifetime defect: a corrupt image leaves the decode offset past the end of the buffer
shape: read past the end of the record
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator: upstream's own regression image, run statement by statement through the in-domain memfs. One caveat worth stating, checked 2026-10-16: the consumer is fts5_decode, a diagnostic SQL function that applications do not normally call. It is registered UNCONDITIONALLY, at sqlite3.c:200679 inside sqlite3Fts5IndexInit, not behind SQLITE_TEST, so it is callable by anyone with SQL access and the reachability is real; but the threat model is narrower than for a case on an ordinary query path

sublet.oracle: VM HALTED on a capability fault, cause 24 untagged dereference (temporal: revoked, or never a capability) pc=0x800239e4 -- taken outside the domain, so cooperative recovery has no frame to return through; all 28 halts in this arm are at the same kernel pc 0x800239e4

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completes, the mechanism reports nothing. 2026-10-06, CheriBSD 15.0-CURRENT riscv64-purecap, memsys5, one boot; the run's positive control gate was satisfied before any case ran

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, memsys5 stock over its static arena (tools/arms.json virtual-sqlite-memsys5): a fault in the function host ASan reported (fault_sites), or the case returns and this arm did not see it
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: reached (the case began (BEGIN line; no marker at the access on this harness)) and completed with no fault

virtual-nested-pools.verdict_note: cause=28 pc=0x3f93221e8c in sqlite3Fts5GetVarint32; by function: sqlite3Fts5GetVarint32 is where host ASan reported it

status: re-measured 2026-10-16 on this platform and every verdict holds. virtual-malloc MISSED, RETURNED, both controls as declared. virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT, cause=28 pc=0x3f86221e8c in sqlite3Fts5GetVarint32 -- cause 28 is CAP_OOB, the bounds check, the right code for a spatial over-read and not the cause 25 the temporal cases turn on -- both controls as declared. cheribsd-revocation MISSED, RETURNED rc=0, positive control trapping, and with probe evidence that the site was reached: site 61 reports hits=60 witnesses=26, against hits=13720 witnesses=4765 from the arm's own site 19 on 2026-10-04/05 (a much wider hook; this one is filtered to the last four bytes of each buffer). The earlier physical readings stand: spatial completes; sublet VM HALTED on a capability fault, cause 24, pc=0x800239e4, one of the 28 halts at that kernel pc, marked in results/matrix.tsv. THE CHERIBSD READING HAD TO BE REPAIRED BEFORE IT MEANT ANYTHING; see note. The arms block is the 2026-10-11 bundle's and is regenerated by derive-verdicts.py when this review ends. RE-MEASURED 2026-10-17 with one arena on every arm (arena_bytes=1048576) and every arm built from the corpus case.c: virtual-malloc MISSED, virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT cause=28 pc=0x3f96221e8c in sqlite3Fts5GetVarint32, cheribsd-revocation MISSED with RETURNED rc=0 and probe site 61 reporting hits=46 witnesses=12 -- reached and silent, not a no-reading. The earlier spatial readings were taken with the virtual arms at a 1 MiB header default against CheriBSD's 262144, and with this arm compiling its own copy of the case
note: Re-measured 2026-10-16; no verdict changes, and the review's finding here is about the CheriBSD arm's tooling rather than this case. The first run of the case on that arm today came back open_rc=0, s1_rc=1, 'no such table: t1_data', RETURNED rc=0 -- and probe site 61 reported hits=0, so the defect site had never been reached. The cause: this arm's copy of the case opens the corrupt image as an ordinary FILE (#define DBPATH /root/corpus/<tag>.db, because CheriBSD has a real VFS where the Capstone arm uses an in-domain memfs), those files existed only inside the guest, nothing in the repository created them, and deploy-corpus.sh begins with rm -rf /root/corpus -- which this review ran today. The failure is silent: sqlite3_open on a missing path CREATES an empty database and returns SQLITE_OK, the first statement returns 'no such table', the case prints RETURNED rc=0, and the runner scores a clean completion. Nine of the 33 cases open such a file -- 00, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, the whole spatial group -- so one redeploy can turn that entire column into clean completions with nothing in the log disagreeing. Fixed at the root: ports/sqlite/cheribsd/make-db-images.py regenerates the images from the byte arrays in the corpus case sources, which are in git and are the same bytes the Capstone arm serves, and writes them into $WORK/out, which deploy-corpus.sh already ships; deploy-corpus.sh now calls it before building the tarball, so a wiped /root/corpus is restored by a redeploy. Four images this arm opens have no corpus source, because those four tags were moved out of the corpus on 2026-10-06 as not-in-scope, and the tool names them rather than failing silently. The campaign readings themselves are not in doubt: the arm's own probe recorded hits=13720 witnesses=4765 for this case on 2026-10-04/05, so the images were present then. With them back, the case reaches the defect -- integrity_check returns SQLITE_CORRUPT (s0_rc=11) as a corrupt image should, the fts5_decode statement runs, and site 61 reports hits=60 witnesses=26, so the over-read happens 26 witnessed times and this arm says nothing. The statement then ends in SQLITE_NOMEM (s1_rc=7), because the 256 KiB arena cannot hold fts5_decode's output for a 40 KiB image; that is after the defect site is reached and so does not affect the reading, but it is recorded because it would make the row a NO-READING if the site count were zero. What site 61 measures is the defect stated as an inequality: fts5DecodePoslist loops while iOff<n and then calls fts5GetVarint32(&a[iOff],...), which may read five bytes, so the hook fires when n-iOff<5 and prints iOff, n, the bytes remaining and whether the first byte carries a continuation bit
fault_sites_why: Host ASan, running the same case source on stock 3.22.0, reports the invalid access in sqlite3Fts5GetVarint32 (live_proof); that run is independent of the Capstone arms and predates them.
